_comment: Everything specific to ONE department lives here. Nothing in src/ or test/ may name an activity or a
weekday - a test enforces that (test/seams.test.mjs), because another department will run its own copy
of this app with its own file and a hardcoded name would be a defect, not a preference.
Weekdays are INTEGERS on purpose: 0=Sunday .. 6=Saturday, matching JS getUTCDay(). The human-readable
name is a translation, so it belongs in strings/, not here.
*** THE ITEMS NUMBERED BELOW ARE PLACEHOLDERS, NOT DESCRIPTIONS OF 4WATER. ***
This announced a count of two, listed three, and then summarised them with a word meaning 'the two of them' -
prose that went stale the moment a third item was added. Same failure as the throttle comment that counted
endpoints and was wrong for an entire increment, here in the one file an operator is told to hand-edit.
A test now checks that any count in this comment matches the list. Describe the list; do not tally it.
It also bans the word meaning 'the two of them' whenever the list is not two, and that ban is deliberately
BLUNT: the original stale sentence paired that word with 'are editable' and named no placeholder at all,
so a rule narrowed to lines mentioning placeholders would miss the exact bug it exists for. Note this very
paragraph cannot quote the word either - the check reads prose and cannot tell a quotation from a claim.
When it fires on innocent prose, reword the prose.
IT ALSO CLAIMED THE CLOCK TIMES WERE INVENTED, AND THEY ARE NOT. The discovery spec's section 1 - the part
read from the real export - states: Wednesdays 19:00 (Salsa, Bachata), 20:15 (DJ); Sundays 13:00-16:00, all
Salsa and Bachata. So Wednesday 19:00 was sourced all along and this file called it a guess, while the 20:15
DJ slot WAS stated and was missing entirely - a weekly DJ shift the app would never have scheduled. The rhythm
above is corrected. The lesson is the one that keeps recurring here: a provenance claim is a claim, and this one
went unchecked because nothing reads the spec except a person deciding to.
AND THE WEDNESDAY DOES NOT RUN THE DANCES TOGETHER. 4water say it ALTERNATES - salsa one week, bachata the next.
The export lists the dances against that slot, which is true of the slot across a season and false of any single
Wednesday, and reading it as a weekly double bill doubled that shift for the whole season. It is separate entries now,
each everyNth 2, the second offset by a week. The same trap as the provenance claim above: a source can be
quoted accurately and still be read into the wrong shape, and nothing catches that except asking.
WHICH DANCE FALLS IN THE FIRST WEEK IS CONFIRMED: salsa. 4water checked it against the real rhythm, so
weekOffset 0 is salsa on purpose rather than as a placeholder. Swapping the activities lines would put every
evening of the season on the wrong dance, so leave the offsets alone unless 4water say the rhythm changed.
SUNDAY IS FOUR ONE-HOUR SLOTS, AND THAT IS 4WATER'S ANSWER, not a reading of the export. Asked and answered
2026-08-23: 13-14, 14-15, 15-16, 16-17. It was a single 15:00 slot standing in for the stated 13:00-16:00
range while the question was open, and it is no longer a placeholder.
Note what that does to the provenance above: the export states 13:00-16:00 and these four slots end at 17:00,
so 4water's answer EXTENDS the export by an hour rather than merely subdividing it. Recorded as their
correction, not as a re-reading of the source, because those are different claims and this file has already
been wrong once about which it was making.
Salsa and Bachata run SIMULTANEOUSLY in each slot, which is why every slot names each of them: a volunteer says
they are free and the planner decides which dance they take, since many can teach either. The four slots exist
to make availability answerable at the hour, which is the granularity availability_hour already stores.
NOTHING IN THIS FILE IS A PLACEHOLDER ANY MORE. Every value is either read from 4water's export or answered
by 4water directly, and _openQuestions below is empty. The numbered list that used to live here is gone
because there is nothing left to number - do not re-add one to hold a value somebody is merely unsure about.
That list meant 'nobody has decided', not 'worth double-checking'.
calendar.eventMinutes is 60, ANSWERED 2026-08-24, and it was implicit in the slots all along: 13-14, 14-15,
15-16 and 16-17 are one-hour slots, so a shift is one hour. It sat at an invented 90 while the question was
treated as open, which it had stopped being. The code default in config.mjs is still 90 for a config that
omits the key - a fallback for somebody else's department, not a statement about this one.
locale is 'en', ANSWERED 2026-08-24: 4water do not need Danish. That settles who reads this and it does NOT
settle export.csvDelimiter, which is ';' for a different reason one line apart in this file - a spreadsheet
splits a .csv on the locale's list separator, and the people opening it are on a Danish Windows whatever
language the interface is in. Two facts that look like one: changing the interface language is not a reason
to touch the delimiter.
The clock times and the timeslots are editable from the Administration screen; the rest is edited here.
ACTIVITIES WITH NO WEEKLY SLOT can never be scheduled: sessions come only from the weekly rhythm, so an
activity no entry names has no dates, no slots and nobody on it. sh, workshop_other and workshop_yoga are in
that position deliberately - the export's recurring pattern does not place them - and a test requires each one
to be declared rather than merely absent. A one-off date for one of them is NOT expressible today: adding a
weekly entry recurs every week of the season.
export.csvDelimiter is a SEMICOLON here, and that is not a typo. A spreadsheet splits a double-clicked
.csv on the locale's list separator, which on a Danish Windows is ';' - so a comma-separated file arrives
with every row crammed into one cell. The code default is ',' because that is what RFC 4180 says and what
Google Sheets, LibreOffice and pandas expect; this line is the deployment saying who actually opens the
file. A department whose people use Sheets or a script should set it back to ','.
The export also carries a UTF-8 byte-order mark, which is not configurable: without it a spreadsheet reads
the downloaded file in the system codepage and 'Soren Norgard' with Danish letters comes out as mojibake.
_openQuestions AND _settledQuestions BELOW ARE THE MACHINE-READABLE FORM OF THE NUMBERED LIST ABOVE.
The prose is for you; those two arrays are for test/docs.test.mjs, which requires every document that
describes this list to mark each entry with an HTML comment naming the id - <!--ph:locale--> and so on -
and to name nothing that has been settled. _openQuestions may be EMPTY, which is the state today and means
the documents must name no open question at all - a test asserts that too, in either direction.
Prose was the only record before, and three documents spent weeks calling the clock times invented after
this file had established they never were.

board._comment: Vagtbørs rules. cutoffDays is spec Q18, DECIDED: a week's notice, so there is realistic time to find a replacement before the shift. It was 2 as a placeholder while the question was open. `requiresApproval` used to sit here and was read by NOTHING: setting it to true would have looked like turning on approval-before-claim and done nothing at all. Removed rather than left as a switch wired to no lamp; if 4water wants approval on claims, that is a feature and not a setting.

retention._comment: Set by the board — see docs/PRIVACY.md. seasons: how many seasons of history to keep (the current one is never removed). notificationDays: how long to keep sent messages, which contain names.

holidays._comment: No sessions are created on a public holiday. country is ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 (DK, FR); an unrecognised one suppresses nothing rather than guessing. extra is for days 4water is closed but the country is not — 24 and 31 December are here as a suggestion and the board can remove them; Grundlovsdag (5 June) is deliberately NOT, because an evening class can run. classesAnyway is the planner's opt-back-in, one date at a time, from the Administration screen.
